To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the instantiation and integration of design patterns are commutable under the following three conditions: (a) the instantiation of the design pattern does not change its interface; (b) the design pattern has a single interface; and (c) the instantiation of design pattern is independent from other design patterns

the instantiation and integration operations of design patterns can be commutated if they are performed on the same design pattern, or if the design pattern being instantiated is not used in the design pattern being integrated.

(1) instantiation of a design pattern is commutable with integration of other design patterns if the design pattern has a single instantiation; (2) instantiation of a pattern is commutable if the instantiation of the pattern is independent of the other patterns that are to be integrated; (3) the order of instantiation and integration does not matter if the instantiation of a pattern does not depend on any other patterns that are integrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: when can a designer instantiate a design pattern and integrate it with other patterns without changing the design outcome?
the following question: Given a design pattern, under what conditions can we change the order of instantiation and integration without changing the final outcome?
the formal specification, analysis, verification, and validation of design patterns and their instantiation and integration processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if a pattern is commutative, the order of its instantiation and integration does not matter.
the commutability depends on whether the design patterns are commutative, and the commutability does not depend on whether the design pattern is instantiated or integrated.
instantiation can be performed before or after integration, but not vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the order in which the two operations are performed is immaterial as long as the design pattern is instantiated before its integration with other patterns.
the commutability is guaranteed when the design patterns are used in a consistent way.
we provide a rigorous mathematical framework to support the design process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a design process can be optimized by reordering these two operations.
the commutability conditions are independent of the design patterns, and they only depend on the design patterns' instantiation interfaces.
a design pattern can be instantiated before or after its integration with other patterns without affecting the final design.
